info.title: cloro
info.description:
API for monitoring AI responses across different providers and regions. One request returns the engine's answer as structured JSON: parsed text, cited sources, brand entities, shopping results, and ads, geo-targeted by country; coverage varies by provider (`GET /v1/countries?model=<provider>` lists it).

## Authentication

Send your API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys are self-serve from the [dashboard](https://dashboard.cloro.dev/api-keys) and every account starts on a free tier of 500 monthly credits. One key grants every endpoint; there are no per-key scopes today.

## Versioning and deprecation

The version is in the URL path. Every endpoint lives under `/v1/`; there is no version header or query parameter.

Within a version, changes are additive: new endpoints, new optional request fields, and new response fields can appear at any time. A client must ignore response fields it does not recognize. A breaking change gets a new version path (`/v2/`) rather than reusing an existing one.

A deprecated endpoint says so in its own responses, not only in a changelog: `Deprecation` (RFC 9745) carries the date the deprecation took effect, `Sunset` (RFC 8594) the date the endpoint stops responding, and a `Link` header with `rel="deprecation"` points at the replacement. There is a minimum of six months between the two dates for any generally available endpoint. Nothing is deprecated today.

## Rate limits

Every authenticated response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, so a client can self-throttle from the response it already has. Scrape endpoints (`/v1/monitor/*` except `/v1/monitor/google/goto`) also send the `X-Concurrency-*` headers once a request passes validation, and the `X-Credits-*` headers on a `200`. Every response carries `X-Request-ID` and `X-Latency-Ms`.

A `429` has one of three codes: `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (one-second window, clears almost immediately), `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (scrape endpoints; clears when your in-flight jobs finish) or `QUEUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (async submission; clears as queued tasks start processing). None carries `Retry-After`, and the IETF `RateLimit-*` header names are not sent.

## Errors

Every 4xx and 5xx response uses the `Error` envelope: `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "timestamp" } }`. `error` is always an object. Branch on `error.code`, a stable machine-readable identifier; `message` is for a human reading a log, and `details` appears only when there is extra context. A `503` (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`) is temporary: retry after the number of seconds in its `Retry-After` header.

post.description:
Return the product panel that a Google Search or Google AI Mode product opens: merchant offers, description, specifications, reviews, images and related products. Send the `productResultToken` from a Google Search `result.shoppingCards` card or `result.aioverview.inlineProducts` entry, or from a Google AI Mode `result.shoppingCards` or `result.inlineProducts` entry.

Costs 1 credit, plus the 2-credit sync surcharge, and only when the request succeeds. A token expires five minutes after the scrape that issued it. If you send the request async, set a high `priority`, so that the token does not expire in the queue.

delete.description: Deletes every task still in the `QUEUED` state for the authenticated organization, letting you drain a pending backlog in one call instead of opening a support request. Tasks that are already `PROCESSING` are in-flight on a worker and are left untouched, as are `COMPLETED` and `FAILED` tasks. Queued tasks have not been charged, so clearing them does not affect your credit balance. The call is safe to repeat — if the queue is already empty it simply returns `cleared: 0`.

ChatGPT currently shows ads only in answers to a follow-up prompt, and far more often on the legacy interface: send `prompt` as an array with `legacy: true`. Paid add-on: one flat +2 credits covers any combination of `rawResponse`, `searchQueries`, `ads` and `shopping` ([pricing](/guides/providers#chatgpt-additional-features)).

shopping.description: Include shopping cards and inline products with pricing and offers. Paid add-on: one flat +2 credits covers any combination of `rawResponse`, `searchQueries`, `ads` and `shopping` ([pricing](/guides/providers#chatgpt-additional-features)).

productDetails.description: Add the rationale and reviews from each product's sheet as `productDetails`. Needs `shopping`. +2 credits on top of `shopping`.

legacy.description: Serve ChatGPT's legacy desktop interface instead of the default mobile-web one. The legacy interface streams the answer as an event stream, so `result.model`, `result.searchQueries` and `result.mapSearchQueries` are populated. ChatGPT shows ads far more often on this interface. Best-effort and temporary: OpenAI controls which interface it serves and can retire the legacy one at any time, so a request can still come back in the mobile-web shape. Handle both. Defaults to false.

disableWebSearch.description: Do not force ChatGPT's web search. cloro returns the answer ChatGPT gives on its own, which uses web search only when ChatGPT decides to, so `result.sources`, `result.citationPills` and `result.searchQueries` are often empty. Defaults to false: web search is forced on every request.

citationPills.description: Inline citation pills extracted from the Gemini answer. Omitted from `result` when the answer carries no pills.

query.description: The search query to execute on Google. Required unless you supply 'url' instead — the two are mutually exclusive.

url.description: A complete Google web search URL to run instead of building the request from 'query' and the targeting fields. Must be an absolute http(s) URL on a Google web search host (google.com, google.co.uk, www.google.de, ...), with the path '/search' and a non-empty 'q'. Mutually exclusive with 'query', 'location', 'uule' and 'pages' — the URL owns those values. cloro applies a fixed set of query parameters — 'q', 'gl', 'hl', 'uule', 'num' (read as result depth), 'start', 'tbs' and 'safe' — and drops anything else. URLs carrying 'tbm' are rejected, because they target a Google vertical with its own endpoint and pricing (use POST /v1/monitor/google/news for tbm=nws).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for localized search results. See [List of countries](/api-reference/endpoint/countries) for the codes each provider supports. Required in the standard request shape unless you send `gl`. When you supply 'url' instead, country is derived from the URL's 'gl' — pass it explicitly to override that, or when the URL has no 'gl'.

location.description: Google canonical location name for geo-targeted results, in comma-separated format: 'City,Region,Country' (see https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/reference/data/geotargets for all ~100,000 supported locations). Use alongside 'country' for city-level precision. Mutually exclusive with 'uule' — provide one or the other, not both. Cannot be combined with 'url'. When both `location` and `uule` are omitted, cloro pins results to the country's canonical location (e.g. `Portugal` for `PT`) where it has one; otherwise Google geolocates from the proxy's exit IP.

uule.description: Pre-encoded Google UULE string for precise geo-targeting. Use this when you have a pre-built UULE value instead of a location name. Mutually exclusive with 'location' — provide one or the other, not both. Cannot be combined with 'url'; put 'uule' in the URL's query string instead.

device.description: Device the search is run from. 'desktop' returns the desktop SERP; 'ios' (Safari on iPhone), 'android' (Chrome on Android) and 'mobile' (alias for 'android') all return the mobile SERP.

pages.description: Number of search results pages to scrape (1-10). Paid add-on: +2 credits per page after the first ([pricing](/guides/providers#google-search-multi-page-pricing)). Cannot be combined with 'url' — in that shape, depth comes from the URL's 'num' (rounded up to whole pages of 10, capped at 10 pages).

citationPills.description: Inline citation chips in the AI summary. Each entry is one (chip, source) pair: when a chip cites N sources, the array has N entries with the same `citationPillId`. Group by `citationPillId` to get the chips. Omitted when the summary has no chips.

label.description: Title of the cited source, the same as its `label` in `sources`
label.example: How Do You Remove Rust from Cast Iron Without Damaging It?

citationPillId.description: 1-based ordinal that all entries from the same chip share

url.description: Direct URL of the cited source

domain.description: Host extracted from `url`, for grouping and display

markdown.description: The AI Overview formatted as Markdown, with each chip replaced by links to its sources. Only when `include.aioverview.markdown` is `true`
markdown.example: ## **Rust can be safely removed from cast iron using abrasives, vinegar, or salt...

html.description: A URL to the full HTML of the results page that Bing rendered. Only when `include.html` is `true`

prompt.description: The prompt to send to Bing AI Mode. Bing puts the prompt in the page URL, so the limit is 3,500 characters after URL encoding. A letter, digit or space counts as 1, most punctuation as 3, an accented or Cyrillic letter as 6, and a Chinese, Japanese or Korean character as 9. Thus a CJK prompt can have a maximum of 388 characters. A longer prompt returns a 400 error: "Prompt is too long (max 3,500 characters, fewer for non-Latin scripts)".
prompt.example: What are the best running shoes for beginners?

country.description: Country/region code for localized response, using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes. Bing AI Mode accepts all countries except CN, KR and RU. `GET /v1/countries?model=bing_aimode` returns the list.

include.description: Optional flags for including additional response formats

html.description: Include a URL to the full HTML of the page that Bing rendered

markdown.description: Include the answer formatted in Markdown in the result. `result.markdown` is returned only when this is `true`.

text.description: Bing AI Mode's answer as plain text, without citation chips
text.example: For beginners, choose a neutral, well-cushioned road shoe...

sources.description: Sources for the answer: first the pages Bing read, then any other page that a citation chip links. Empty when the answer has no sources.

position.description: 1-based position of the source in this array

label.description: Title of the source page. Can be an empty string.

description.description: Snippet that Bing shows for the source. Omitted when Bing shows none.
description.example: Our test team picked the best shoes for new runners.

citationPills.description: Inline citation chips in the answer. Each entry is one (chip, source) pair: when a chip cites N sources, the array has N entries with the same `citationPillId`. Group by `citationPillId` to get the chips. Empty when the answer has no chips.

position.description: 1-based position of this source in the sibling `result.sources` array.

label.description: Title of the cited source, the same as its `label` in `result.sources`. Can be an empty string.

url.description: Direct URL of the cited source.

domain.description: Host extracted from `url`, for grouping and display.

markdown.description: The answer formatted in Markdown, with citations as links (included when include.markdown is true)

html.description: A URL to the full HTML of the page that Bing rendered (included when include.html is true).

ShoppingCard.description: Shopping product card with detailed product information

ImagePosition.description: Pixel offset for image positioning within a slot

SlotPlacement.description: Percent-based placement of a showcase slot within its container

ShowcaseSlot.description: Single visual slot inside a product showcase

ShowcaseImage.description: Image rendered as the hero of a product showcase

ShowcaseBackground.description: Background styling for a product showcase

ShowcaseMetadata.description: Visual showcase metadata attached to a shopping product (image, background, and per-slot placement).

slots.description: Slot map keyed by slot identifier

debug.description: Free-form debug metadata; opaque to clients

title.example: Nike Court Vision Low Next Nature Shoes

position.description: 1-indexed rank across all products in all shopping cards in the response (flat, not reset per card).

description.description: Product description
description.example: Classic sneaker with modern comfort features

subtitle.description: gpt-6 product card with no listing: the line under the card title

attributes.description: gpt-6 product card: the "Label: value" lines of the card, such as "Best for: ..."

value.example: one or two monitors and daily work

citationPillIds.description: gpt-6 product card: the `citationPillId` of each citation chip in the card. The pills are in `result.citationPills`; look them up by `citationPillId`. Omitted when the card has no citation.

kind.description: Inline product: what the card is. `product`: a shop product. It has a listing (`id`, `offers`) or a product reference in the ChatGPT answer. `entity`: a card whose title is a named entity in the ChatGPT answer, such as a brand, a company, a software or a TV show. `row`: any other card, such as "Coffee capsules". Not on shopping card products.

entityCategory.description: Inline product: the category that ChatGPT gives to the entity in the card title, such as `brand`, `software`, `local_business` or `tv_show`. ChatGPT sets the values, and new values can occur. `null` when the card title has no entity. Not on shopping card products.

ctaLinks.description: Inline product: the merchant links on the call-to-action lines of the gpt-6 product card, such as "Acheter chez TennisPro". A citation chip, an offer of the product sheet and a link in the card text are not call-to-action links. An empty array when the card has no call-to-action line, and on an inline product that is not a gpt-6 card. Not on shopping card products.

price.description: Current price. On a gpt-6 card with no listing, the price text of the card. A line with no currency, such as a rating or an address, is not a price.

offers.description: Shopping offers with pricing details from different merchants

product_lookup_key.description: Key used to look up product updates

request_query.description: Search query used for this product

generatedProductQuery.description: Broad shopping query ChatGPT generated for this product (extracted from product_lookup_key.data). Useful for understanding the search intent behind the recommendation.
generatedProductQuery.example: best microwaves uk 2026 countertop inverter combi microwave

ShoppingOffer.description: Shopping offer with pricing details from a specific merchant

brand.description: Product brand. Set on only some offers, so often `null` or absent.

product_name.description: Product name as listed by merchant
product_name.example: Nike Men's Court Vision Low Next Nature Shoes

price.description: Offer price

checkoutable.description: Whether the product can be checked out directly

is_digital.description: Whether this is a digital product

PriceDetails.description: Detailed price breakdown for an offer

RatingGroupedCitation.description: Rating source information with supporting websites

title.example: Nike Men's Court Vision Low Next Nature Shoes

InlineProduct.description: Inline product reference that appeared in the response text, or a product card of a gpt-6 answer, including pricing and offers

render_as.description: How the product is rendered in the response. Absent for a gpt-6 product card.

ProductReview.description: One review source from the product sheet

rating.description: Rating at the source. Not returned at the moment.

numReviews.description: Number of reviews at the source. Not returned at the moment.

citeUrl.description: URL of the source. Not returned at the moment.

StateParameter.description: State code for sub-country geo-targeting (e.g., "CA"). Only valid with country "US". Paid add-on: +2 credits, on top of the base cost and any other add-on ([pricing](/guides/providers#state-level-targeting)).

GlParameter.description: Alternative to `country`, using Google's own parameter name for the result geography. Same ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, accepted in either case (`us` or `US`), and must be a country the endpoint supports — see `GET /v1/countries`. Provide `country` or `gl`; sending both with different values is a `400`.

HlParameter.description: Interface language, as Google's own `hl` parameter (e.g. `en`, `de`, `pt-BR`). Free-form and case-insensitive — Google owns the list of codes. Overrides the language cloro derives from the country, so the interface language and the result geography can differ.

GooglePlaceBase.description: Fields shared by the place and map entries of a Google AI answer

index.description: Position index of the place in the results

address.description: Full postal address, as Google gives it on the card's Directions link

placeId.description: Google Knowledge Graph ID for the place. A place and its `map` entry share it. Omitted when Google did not geo-tag the card.

phone.description: Phone number from the card's Call button, formatted as Google ships it for the locale. Omitted when the card has no Call button.

website.description: Business website from the card's Website button. Omitted when the card has no Website button.

GooglePlace.description: Place card from a Google AI answer

link.description: Google viewer URL for the place. It is the URL of the place's entry in `sources`. Omitted when `sources` has no entry for the place.

GoogleMapPlace.description: Place card from a Google AI answer that Google geo-tagged

link.description: Google Maps URL for the place

ProductDetails.description: Rationale and reviews from the product sheet

productResultToken.description: The `productResultToken` from a Google Search shopping card or AI Overview inline product, or from a Google AI Mode shopping card or inline product. The token carries the query, locale and location of the request that issued it, so the request takes no other field.

productResults.description: One entry: the product panel of the card that issued the token. Same shape as Google Search and AI Mode `productResults`. Only `title` is always present.

position.description: 1-indexed rank across the `inlineProducts` array in DOM/render order.

price.description: Price as displayed. Fields that can't be parsed are omitted, never sent as `null`. When Google supplies structured price data, `currency` is an ISO code (`USD`) and `raw` appears only if the page also showed the price text.

currency.description: Currency symbol as displayed, or an ISO code when Google supplies structured price data

oldPrice.description: Original price before discount. Same shape as `price`.

currency.description: Currency symbol as displayed, or an ISO code when Google supplies structured price data

rating.description: Average rating out of 5, from Google's product data. Absent when Google shows no rating.

productResultToken.description: Token for [`POST /v1/monitor/google/product`](/api-reference/endpoint/google/product), which returns the product panel that this product opens. Expires five minutes after the scrape. Present only when the product links to a Google product panel.

ProductDocid.description: Google's ID for the product, read from `productLink`. The same product has the same value in `shoppingCards`, `inlineProducts` and `productResults` of one response. Google can change the value between responses, so do not use it to identify a product over time. Absent when the link from Google has no ID.

ProductResult.description: One product cluster and its merchant offers. Only `title` is guaranteed; anything Google's panel lacks is omitted, never sent as `null`.

title.description: Product cluster title, as Google displayed it. Empty when the page has no product heading.

stores.description: Merchant offers. Always present on Google Search entries; omitted on AI Mode when Google lists none.

link.description: Merchant product URL, passed through from Google verbatim

redirectLink.description: Google's `/goto` redirect for this link, in the absolute form `POST /v1/monitor/google/goto` accepts. Present only when Google served the link as a redirect. The sibling link field holds the destination cloro resolved it to, or is empty, missing or a `google.com/goto` URL when the link is not resolved yet. In that case, resolve this value with `POST /v1/monitor/google/goto`.

price.description: Offer price. Omitted when the displayed text can't be parsed.

value.description: Parsed numeric price. On installment offers, the monthly payment.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, or the displayed token when it maps to none

description.description: Merchant's listing title, naming the exact SKU sold
description.example: iPhone 17 256GB White - Apple

buyingOptions.description: Merchant badges in display order, such as stock status, delivery promise and returns window

shipping.description: Shipping cost or promise as displayed

description.description: Prose blurb

specifications.description: Spec tables: each category name maps to key/value pairs. Category names and keys arrive in the response language.

productDocid.description: Google's ID for the product, equal to the `productDocid` of the shopping card or inline product that this entry came from. Present only when the product came from a Google AI Mode shopping card or inline product. A product from a Google Search shopping card does not have it.

bearerAuth.description: cloro API key as a bearer token. One key grants every endpoint in this spec; per-key scopes are not available, so a client cannot request a narrower permission. Keys are created and revoked in the [dashboard](https://dashboard.cloro.dev/api-keys).

XRateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed in the current window.

XRateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

XRequestId.description: Unique ID for this request. Support uses it to find your request.

XLatencyMs.description: Milliseconds the API spent on the request, from arrival to the start of the response. Excludes network transit.
